prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
[goal] Fix the hook bus so `tool.after` hooks run in order, always run, and failures propagate.

[action] Rewrote `emit` in `src/bus.ts`. The old code was `list.forEach(async (handler) => { await handler(payload); })` — `forEach` ignores the async callback, so all handlers started at once (out of order), `emit` resolved immediately (before any handler finished), and handler rejections became unhandled promise rejections (silently ignored). The new `emit` snapshots the handler list (so mid-emit unsubscribe/subscribe doesn't change who runs this emit, per README line 13-14) and awaits each handler in a plain `for...of` loop, so the loop stops and `emit` rejects with the first handler error.

[result]
- Public API unchanged: `on` (returns unsubscribe), `emit`, `count`; no new dependencies; `test/bus.test.ts` untouched — `npm test` passes 2/2.
- Verified the full README contract with a scratch script (12/12 ok, then deleted): strict subscription order with overlapping async handlers; `emit` unresolved until handlers finish; sync throw and async rejection both reject `emit` with the same error and skip later handlers; self-unsubscribing handler still runs its own emit and is gone on the next; the audit plugin scenario (one-time notice → async redaction → audit log) runs in the documented order.

[found] One bug, in `emit` only: fire-and-forget `forEach(async …)`. That single line explains all three reports — out-of-order execution, "hooks never running" (emit resolved before they finished, so callers moved on / results weren't redacted yet), and silently ignored failures (unhandled rejections).

[assumptions] README is the spec (it says "the README there says how the bus must behave"), so I kept `on`'s semantics exactly as-is; the plugin needed no changes — its behavior was correct, it was just starved by the broken bus.
